title: Why Hitachi’s heavy-welding lines are busy: the mining-truck wave behind the workload
summary: The strongest public explanation for the current workload is a concentrated wave of ultra-class mining equipment deliveries rather than a broad construction boom. Hitachi Construction Machinery has disclosed 42 additional EH4000AC-3 trolley dump trucks for Zambia, 30 more dump trucks for gold mines in Australia and Uzbekistan, and two EX8000-7 ultra-large excavators for Peru, with deliveries starting in FY2026. Its FY2026 mining forecast is ¥482.5 billion, up 14%, while new mining dump-truck revenue is forecast to jump 75%.
why_it_matters: For welders and fabrication teams making large frames, booms, arms, buckets, track frames and truck structures, the important signal is timing: Hitachi booked only ¥4.2 billion of new mining-truck revenue in Q1 but forecasts ¥36.7 billion for the full year, leaving ¥32.5 billion for Q2-Q4. Some Americas truck shipments have also slipped into FY2027 without cancellation, so part of the load extends beyond this fiscal year. Hitachi does not publicly disclose plant-level overtime by order, so the link to a specific shop's OT should be treated as a strong workload inference, not a confirmed management statement.

claims.text: Hitachi Construction Machinery disclosed orders for 42 additional EH4000AC-3 trolley dump trucks for the Kansanshi copper mine in Zambia, two EX8000-7 excavators for a Peru copper mine, and 30 dump trucks for mines in Australia and Uzbekistan, with phased deliveries starting in FY2026.

Hitachi forecasts FY2026 mining revenue of ¥482.5 billion, up 14% year on year; new mining dump-truck revenue is forecast at ¥36.7 billion, up 75%, and new mining excavator revenue at ¥79.8 billion, up 8%.
Only ¥4.2 billion of new mining dump-truck revenue was recorded in Q1, while ¥32.5 billion is forecast for Q2-Q4.
claims.basis: FY2026 Q1 actual and full-year forecast charts.

claims.text: Hitachi raised the Asia/Oceania outlook for both mining excavators and dump trucks; some Americas dump-truck shipments were shifted into FY2027 and the company explicitly said this was not due to lost orders.

Across the Hitachi group, welded mining structures include excavator fronts such as booms, arms and buckets, track frames, and rigid-dump-truck bodies; the EH4000AC-3 itself uses fabricated box-section and rectangular frame rails and has a 221-tonne nominal payload.
claims.basis: Hitachi manufacturing release and EH4000AC-3 product specification.

claims.text: Kansanshi's S3 expansion entered commercial production at the end of 2025, and First Quantum guides Kansanshi copper output from 175–205 kt in 2026 to 210–240 kt in 2027 and 230–260 kt in 2028.
Hitachi targets Latin American mining excavator share rising from 26% in 2024 to 30% in 2028 and mining dump-truck share from 4% to 18%; it also targets ¥700 billion of mining revenue by 2030.
claims.basis: Hitachi's 2026 regional strategy and medium-term strategy materials.

claims.text: Hitachi aims to commercialize its full-battery mining dump truck in FY2027 after a Zambia trial exceeded 4,000 km and 30,000 tonnes hauled.

At Barrick's Lumwana copper mine, 24 Hitachi EH5000 trucks are currently operating, while Barrick's Super Pit plan calls for total mining volumes to rise from about 150 Mt in 2025 to about 240 Mt in 2028 and roughly 290 Mt per year from 2030.
claims.basis: Hitachi installed-base disclosure and Barrick expansion plan.

claims.text: The IEA's 2026 outlook projects a roughly 25% copper supply deficit in 2035 under its base project pipeline and says copper has the largest volume demand growth among key critical minerals through 2040.

The unusually heavy FY2026–FY2027 fabrication load is better explained by a concentrated hard-rock mining delivery wave and specific project wins than by a uniform boom across all Hitachi construction-equipment markets.
claims.basis: Large named mining orders, back-loaded truck revenue, shipment spillover, and mine-expansion production ramp.

claims.text: The public data supports continued heavy mining-machine workload through at least FY2027, but it does not prove the exact amount of overtime at any individual Japanese welding shop or that every ordered structure will be fabricated in Japan.
claims.basis: Hitachi publishes order and revenue timing but not plant-level overtime allocation; welded structures are also produced within its overseas network.

claims.text: Lumwana is a credible future sales opportunity for Hitachi because of its large installed EH5000 fleet and sharply rising material-movement requirements, but no new Lumwana Hitachi truck order is assumed here.
claims.basis: Installed-base relationship plus mine expansion; no cited source announces a new order.

content.key_message: The near-term workload signal is unusually strong for Hitachi's mining-machine fabrication chain: large named orders are entering delivery, FY2026 dump-truck revenue is heavily back-loaded into Q2-Q4, and some shipments already extend into FY2027. The longer-term case is supported by copper-mine expansion and Hitachi's aggressive mining-share targets, but those are forecasts and targets rather than guaranteed shop hours.
whats_new: Hitachi's biggest disclosed mining orders begin delivering in FY2026: 42 trolley trucks for Kansanshi, 30 additional dump trucks for gold mines, and two EX8000-7 excavators for Peru.
The Q1 numbers hide the coming production load: new mining-truck revenue was only ¥4.2 billion in Q1, versus ¥32.5 billion forecast across Q2-Q4.
Some Americas truck deliveries have moved into FY2027 without cancellation, creating visible workload spillover instead of a clean March 2027 cutoff.
Latin America is now an explicit conquest market: Hitachi wants dump-truck share there to move from 4% to 18% by 2028.
why_now: Kansanshi is not merely replacing old trucks. Its S3 expansion reached commercial production and copper output is planned to climb through 2028, requiring more ore and waste movement.
Hitachi is concentrating on hard-rock copper and gold projects where ultra-class trucks and excavators carry very high equipment value and large fabricated structures.
The company's own FY2026 forecast shows mining-machine revenue accelerating after Q1, consistent with large units moving through fabrication, assembly and shipment later in the year.

what_workers_are_building_for.job: Hauls ore and waste in open-pit mines; the trolley system can draw power from overhead lines on equipped haul roads.
what_workers_are_building_for.scale: 221-tonne nominal payload and 384-tonne gross machine operating weight.
what_workers_are_building_for.welding_relevance: Its frame uses fabricated box-section and rectangular rails designed to resist bending and torsional loads.

what_workers_are_building_for.job: High-volume loading of mining trucks at large open-pit mines.
what_workers_are_building_for.welding_relevance: Large excavator fronts and undercarriage structures require heavy fabrication; Hitachi identifies booms, arms, buckets and track frames among mining welded structures produced in its group.

hidden_signal.headline: The biggest signal is the gap between Q1 and the rest of FY2026.
hidden_signal.detail: Hitachi recorded only ¥4.2 billion of new mining dump-truck revenue in Q1 but forecasts ¥36.7 billion for FY2026. That leaves ¥32.5 billion—almost 89% of the year's truck revenue—to be recognized after June. For people on fabrication and assembly lines, this is more useful than the consolidated headline because it tells you when the large-unit work has to flow.
hidden_signal.caution: Revenue timing is not identical to welding hours; fabrication can occur before accounting recognition and production is shared across sites and suppliers.

forecast.reason: Named FY2026 deliveries plus a ¥32.5 billion Q2-Q4 new-truck revenue plan.
Some Americas truck shipments have already shifted into FY2027 without cancellations; Kansanshi production continues climbing; Hitachi targets FY2027 commercialization of its battery truck.

Hitachi targets ¥700 billion mining revenue by 2030 and a major Latin American truck-share increase, while copper mine investment remains structurally supported. These are targets and market conditions, not booked backlog.

next_wave_to_watch.why: It already runs 24 Hitachi EH5000 trucks, while Barrick plans to raise mining volumes sharply as the Super Pit expands. That creates a logical replacement/expansion opportunity for ultra-class haulage equipment.
next_wave_to_watch.important_caveat: This article does not count Lumwana as a new Hitachi order. It is an addressable opportunity, and competing manufacturers are active in large copper fleets.

risks: Mine expansion delays or lower commodity prices can push equipment deliveries out by quarters or years.
Hitachi itself says competition is severe in parts of North America and Australian coal; not every mining segment is equally strong.
Regional production sharing means a global order does not translate one-for-one into hours at a specific Japanese welding site.
The 2030 mining-revenue and Latin American share figures are management targets, not guaranteed orders.
Tariffs, materials and transportation costs can alter production schedules and margins even when customer demand remains intact.
what_to_watch_next: Hitachi's FY2026 Q2 results in late October 2026: check whether the ¥32.5 billion Q2-Q4 mining-truck plan is still intact.
Any additional EH4000/EH5000 or EX5600/EX8000 orders from Zambia, Peru, Chile or Australia.
Whether FY2027 shipment deferrals grow further or begin converting to deliveries.
New hiring, shifts or supplier capacity announcements at Hitachinaka/Tsuchiura and major fabrication suppliers.
Commercial orders for the FY2027 full-battery dump truck after the Kansanshi demonstration.
content.skeptical_view: There is no public Hitachi disclosure saying 'overtime increased because of these exact orders.' Plant-level OT, work allocation and supplier splits are internal. The correct conclusion is narrower: public orders and revenue timing strongly support a heavy mining-machine production wave, and the timing matches the kind of work that would pressure fabrication and assembly capacity.

30 sec.what_happened: Hitachi has a wave of very large mining-machine orders entering production and delivery.
30 sec.why_it_matters: Its full-year mining-truck forecast is heavily back-loaded: ¥4.2B in Q1 versus ¥32.5B planned for Q2-Q4, with some shipments already moving into FY2027.
30 sec.what_to_do_watch: Watch late-October Q2 results for whether the truck forecast holds and whether more copper/gold orders appear.
30 sec.bottom_line: Current heavy-fabrication workload has a credible order-driven explanation, and the strongest evidence says it should not disappear immediately after this fiscal year.

reading_levels.2 min: Hitachi's mining workload is being pulled by a small number of very large hard-rock projects. The disclosed list includes 42 additional EH4000AC-3 trolley trucks for First Quantum's expanding Kansanshi copper mine, 30 dump trucks for Australian and Uzbek gold mines, and two EX8000-7 excavators for Peru. The accounting pattern is even more revealing: only ¥4.2 billion of new mining-truck revenue appeared in Q1, while ¥36.7 billion is planned for the year, leaving ¥32.5 billion for the remaining three quarters. Hitachi also says some Americas deliveries moved into FY2027 without cancellation. Underneath that, Kansanshi's copper output is planned to rise through 2028, Hitachi is trying to multiply its Latin American truck share, and copper supply remains structurally tight. This supports a good near-term and medium-term mining workload picture. It does not prove a specific shop's overtime schedule, and not every global order is fabricated in Japan.

content.recommendation: For workers, treat the current OT surge as order-cycle driven rather than permanent. The strongest visibility runs through FY2026 and into FY2027. If deciding on overtime income, transfers, training or long-term career moves, do not budget as if today's OT is guaranteed through 2030; instead follow the Q2 mining-truck forecast, shipment deferrals and new copper/gold order announcements.
